subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: May synchronous authorization reads ever bypass the exec-approval writer lock, or must the fix preserve a committed-snapshot boundary for every policy decision?
rationale: This is a security-boundary choice: lockless reads may restore availability but can observe an in-place copy fallback unless maintainers choose and enforce a different committed-state contract.

options.title: Require committed-state reads
options.body: Revise the fix so readers consume only an immutable or fully committed snapshot while retaining fail-closed behavior for unavailable policy state.

options.title: Accept constrained lock bypass
options.body: Allow lockless same-process reads only after maintainers explicitly accept the overlap risk and add proof covering every writer publication path.

options.title: Pause this approach
options.body: Close or replace this PR if a safe committed-snapshot repair cannot remain bounded within the exec-approval store.

recommendation.title: Require committed-state reads
recommendation.body: Revise the fix so readers consume only an immutable or fully committed snapshot while retaining fail-closed behavior for unavailable policy state.
